name: Bin Packing Benchmark Dataset
description: This dataset provides 10,000 reproducible instances of the one-dimensional Bin Packing Problem, accompanied by solver-certified integer and linear programming optima, deterministic heuristic packings, optimality certificates, and associated metadata. In the Bin Packing Problem, items with positive integer weights must be assigned to identical bins of a fixed capacity. Every item must be packed exactly once, without exceeding any bin’s capacity. The objective is to minimise the number of bins used. The collection supports computational experiments in combinatorial optimisation, integer programming, linear programming relaxations, approximation algorithms, packing heuristics, and lower-bound techniques. It also provides a resource for algorithm benchmarking and teaching in operations research and computer science. The benchmark includes ten item counts: n = 12, 20, 28, 40, 60, 80, 120, 200, 400, and 800, with bin capacities of 100, 500, or 1,000. Ten instance families are represented: uniform, small-item dominated, large-item dominated, bimodal, clustered, near-half-capacity, near-capacity with fillers, complementary pairs, planted feasible packings, and search-selected quartets. Each family contains 1,000 instances, with 100 at each item count. The search-selected family deliberately targets the recorded heuristics and supports stress testing rather than unbiased estimates of their general performance.
